SEVEN_APPARENT_TIES_ARE_ONE_OUTAGE_NOT_S.what_it_actually_is: all 7 exact ties are the SAME WINDOW -- `*-updown-5m-1787716800` across btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, bnb and hype -- with T staleness 537-538s and t0 staleness 237-238s. BOTH boundary reads returned THE SAME STALE SAMPLE, which is WHY xT == x0. They are one feed outage at one window, not seven independent ties.
SEVEN_APPARENT_TIES_ARE_ONE_OUTAGE_NOT_S.why_the_first_split_was_wrong: my classifier tested `tie` BEFORE `stale`, so precedence decided attribution. All 7 ties are ALSO stale>1s. Corrected: 41 = 31 stale + 10 margin, with the 7 as a NAMED SUBSET of the stale class rather than a class of their own.
SEVEN_APPARENT_TIES_ARE_ONE_OUTAGE_NOT_S.the_lesson_recorded: a residual split is only as good as its class PRECEDENCE. Reporting 24/10/7 would have invented a 'tie' phenomenon out of an outage.
